title: HyperSkill: Training-Free Omnimodal GRPO via Hypergraph-Indexed Skill-Library Evolution
claim: Training the backbone's parameters is costly, forgetful and opaque; freezing it and evolving an external structured skill library avoids this.
layout: 2 panels left-to-right, big arrow between, legend strip along bottom
description: A two-panel figure with a legend strip below. The left panel, outlined in gray and titled "Traditional: Parameter-Space", shows a column of modality icons (text, image, PDF, video, audio) labeled "Multimodal Task". Next to it is a "Trainable Backbone" box with weights [w] and an update Δθ. Below it, a red-outlined "Limitations" box lists Expensive, Forgetful and Opaque, each with an icon. A large blue arrow reading "Freeze, Evolve Skills" leads to the right panel, which has a blue outline. There the same modality icons feed a locked "Frozen Backbone" bar, with a snowflake and library icon beside it. The title reads "HyperSkill: Skill-Library Evolution". A purple box shows a hypergraph of green u>0 nodes and red u<0 nodes joined by hyperedges. Below it are the components C1 Distillation, C2 Gated Retrieval and C3 Execution. The bottom legend explains four icons: Frozen Parameters, Hyperedge Composition, Auditable Skills and Omnimodal Tasks.
caption: Parameter-space GRPO is costly, forgetful and opaque; HyperSkill instead keeps the backbone frozen and evolves a hypergraph-indexed skill library.
abstract: Reinforcement learning sharpens LLM reasoning, but parameter updates are expensive, forgetful, and opaque; training-free libraries swap gradients for a textual store but still use trajectory-level, correlation-based admission and flat structure. To address both, we propose HyperSkill, a Training-Free Omnimodal GRPO framework that keeps the backbone frozen and replaces gradient updates with auditable edits to a Hypergraph-Indexed Skill-Library, where skills are advantage-bearing nodes and compositions are hyperedges. It has three components: training-time distillation admits counterfactually checked skills and learns a protocol skill from failures; gated hypergraph retrieval injects advantage-ranked skills where a per-dataset gate admits them; and an execution protocol makes the frozen backbone commit to an answer. On 11 text, vision-language, and omnimodal benchmarks, HyperSkill is best or tied on every dataset and beats the best baseline by 13.0 average F1 points while keeping the backbone frozen. Our software and data are publicly available at https://github.com/LHRLAB/HyperSkill.
